note: The two sets are nearly identical in coverage of the wiring schedule and bind the same rows and values the same way. Set A states the 32 and 50 entries with specific attributes (conductor specification / conductor configuration) and no spurious conditions, while Set B calls both merely "conductor" and adds "CU" as a condition, which is vague and misplaces the material. Each set carries one claim with a bogus "C"/"C." condition, and both omit the NOTES equipment ratings and several schedule details (150's 3#4/0 and 2-1/2" conduit, 34's 3#10G ground, 151's armored-cable type). On balance A is the cleaner, more faithful set.
remarks: Text layer of the WIRING SCHEDULE is jumbled: symbol numbers and descriptions are interleaved inconsistently (e.g. 150/20/50 vs. their descriptions), so row-to-description binding could only be checked for internal consistency with the image; both sets use the same binding (20=3#12,#12G,3/4"C; 50=3#6,#8G,1"C; 31=2#10,#10G,3/4"C; 32=2#10USE-2; 150=AL 3#4/0,#4G,2-1/2"C; 151=AL 3#4/0 ARMORED CABLE; 10=#12/2WG). Both extractors turn the trailing "C." abbreviation (conduit) in quotes such as 1"C. into a condition. Both sets omit every NOTES fact (120/240V sub-panel with 50A/2P main breaker, 2.8kW inverter with ground fault, 60A DC NFDS, 200A/2P NFDS, NEMA 3R junction box, NEC 690.42 exception) and both repeat the item 50 conductors under two names (conductor count/size 3#6 and conductor configuration 3#6, #8G.).
